archetype: Azorius draw-go control that gifts the whole table cards, taxes and drains them for taking them, forts against combat, and wins with the second cast of Approach of the Second Sun. The commander is the discount engine, not the threat: Heliod, the Warped Eclipse grants flash to every spell and cuts each by {1} for each card opponents drew this turn (oracle text, cards.json), and the eleven symmetrical-draw permanents exist to make that number large. There is no two-card combo — deck-facts finds one contained line (Approach of the Second Sun + Mystical Tutor, bracket 3, mana_value_needed 15, produces 'Win the game') and `two_card_infinites: 0`. The old Aetherflux Reservoir / Hullbreaker Horror kill is gone from cards.json, and the pilot holds a standing constraint against replacing it.

role_assignment.default_role: Control, and the kind that owns the long game outright rather than the kind stalling for a combo. strategy:whos-the-beatdown puts the question as Duke's inevitability test — whoever loses a game that goes long enough must be the beatdown — and strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock names the source: 'superior late-game card quality, an engine that scales, an unanswerable finisher, or simply more answers than the opponent has threats.' This deck has the third and the fourth. Approach of the Second Sun's second cast from hand simply wins (oracle text; verified stack 002, checker.verdict == 'pass'), and it is unanswerable except on the stack. The measured shape agrees: over 120 Forge games on the standard bracket-3 pod, 20 of heliod's 27 wins read won_by "effect of 'Approach of the Second Sun'" and 7 read 'all opponents have lost' — the deck's own record of winning by outliving the table. Mean finishing position 2.319 over 94 ranked games (16 firsts, 43 seconds, 24 thirds, 11 fourths). You are never the beatdown by damage: combat damage dealt to players had mean 4.11 and MEDIAN 0.5, and commander damage reached 21 in zero of 120 games.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: The pivot is the second Approach, and strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window sets the bar for when to take it: the window opens when the attempt 'can't be profitably answered — protection up, table tapped out, interaction counted and accounted for.' Concretely: the first Approach has resolved (it went seventh from the top and you gained 7), you have drawn or tutored to it again, and you can pay {6}{W} — the goldfish's mean available mana crosses 7 between turn 8 (6.966) and turn 9 (7.612), earlier when Heliod's back face is down and the table is drawing, which the goldfish does not model. Before that moment, strategy:pivot-point's instruction is the whole plan: 'hold the protection spell for the turn you commit, not after.' The second cast is the only turn this deck should ever look like it is winning, and strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection prices that: 'the deflection budget spends down as your engine shows; plan the pivot before it runs out.' Ghostly Prison, Propaganda and free cards for the table are the budget.
role_assignment.seat_relative_note: strategy:whos-the-beatdown's Commander correction — role is seat-relative, 'assign per-threat, not per-game.' Against the pod's flier deck you are pure defence: giada-angels dealt 39 of the 74 eliminations heliod suffered, and 53 of them were eliminated_how 'damage'. Against the two grindier seats you are the one accruing, and your one-for-ones should stay in hand (strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry).

engines.engine: THE win condition. First cast resolves, gains 7 life and goes seventh from the top; the second cast from hand wins outright. Everything else in the 99 buys the turns to cast it twice.
engines.evidence: verified stack 002 (checker.verdict == 'pass') resolves exactly when the win is checked and names the stack as the only interaction window; combo_details records Approach + Mystical Tutor, bracket 3, mana_value_needed 15, popularity 21070, produces ['Win the game']; sim run n120: 20 of heliod's 27 wins carry won_by "effect of 'Approach of the Second Sun'"

engines.engine: The discount and the flash grant. 'You may cast spells as though they had flash. Spells you cast cost {1} less to cast for each card your opponents have drawn this turn.' Every symmetric draw permanent is a cost reducer, and flash turns the whole deck into held-up mana.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; flip cost {3}{U/P} on top of {2}{W}{W} — goldfish target 'Heliod plus the mana to flip him' assembles 0.823 of games, 0.642 by turn six, mean turn 4.808; goldfish commander mean_cast_turn 4.221. `model-coverage heliod` lists Heliod's only channel as `bodies` — the discount is NOT modelled, so every goldfish mana figure here is measured with it OFF and is a floor

engines.piece: Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Temple Bell, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Dictate of Kruphix, Mikokoro, Kwain, Loran of the Third Path, The Second Doctor, Scrawling Crawler, Forced Fruition
engines.engine: The symmetric gift: eleven permanents that hand the whole table cards, plus Faerie Mastermind's {3}{U} activation. Enumerated from cards.json oracle text — note that Decanter of Endless Water, which the goldfish target file counts in this group, does NOT make anyone draw ('You have no maximum hand size. {T}: Add one mana of any color'). They are the fuel for Heliod's per-draw discount, the trigger source for every tax below, and the deck's political cover — strategy:multiplayer.politics' 'engineered dilemmas' in permanent form. The Second Doctor makes the gift literally buy peace: each opponent who draws 'can't attack you or permanents you control during their next turn'.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; goldfish target 'Table draw engine online' assembles 0.935 of games, 0.854 by turn six, mean turn 2.319 — the earliest and most reliable target in the file

engines.piece: Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Smothering Tithe, Consecrated Sphinx, Faerie Mastermind, Teferi's Ageless Insight, Alhammarret's Archive
engines.engine: The asymmetry converter. The gift above is symmetric and therefore not card advantage; these seven make it one-sided. strategy:card-advantage's Commander correction is the reason the deck is built this way: 'engines that out-draw three players are the format's defining advantage.' Consecrated Sphinx draws two on EVERY opponent draw — with Howling Mine or Font of Mythos out it reads off the table's own upkeep.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; goldfish target 'Heliod down with an asymmetric card engine' assembles 0.787, 0.581 by turn six; goldfish mean_extra_cards_drawn_by_turn 3.586 at turn ten. Caveat from goldfish meta.card_advantage: 13 cards draw, only 2 are MODELLED, and Sphinx, Remora, Rhystic Study, Faerie Mastermind, Kefnet, Ageless Insight and Psychosis Crawler are all in `draw_not_modelled`

engines.engine: The each-opponent drain that scales with the gift: Psychosis Crawler is 'whenever you draw a card, each opponent loses 1 life' with power equal to your hand size; Scrawling Crawler is 'whenever an opponent draws a card, that player loses 1 life' plus an upkeep draw for everybody. strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry names exactly this shape — 'effects that tax or drain every opponent at once'.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; goldfish target 'Draw-trigger punisher drawn' 0.366 assembled (0.737 with tutors), and 'Engine + punisher assembled' only 0.334 (0.702 assisted), 0.204 by turn six — the deck's least reliable pairing. Sim n120: noncombat damage dealt to players mean 1.68, MEDIAN 0.0. Read the median: this is a value layer, not a clock

engines.piece: Propaganda, Ghostly Prison, Archangel of Tithes
engines.engine: The fort. Three taxers that blank attack plans from three seats at once for one card. strategy:card-advantage.virtual states the multiplier verbatim: 'one tax or pillow-fort effect can blank attack plans from three players at once, the cheapest way to "answer" ~120 life worth of aggression.' Archangel is the only one that taxes and blocks fliers in the same slot.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; goldfish target 'A taxer down' assembles 0.487 (0.791 with tutors), only 0.355 by turn six. Enumerated against the other three defensive targets (blockers 0.750, protection 0.680, held interaction 0.843) it is the least reliable thing keeping you alive; the two punisher targets assemble lower still (0.366 and 0.334) but those are value, not survival

engines.piece: Angelic Wall, Drift of Phantasms, Archangel of Tithes, Consecrated Sphinx, Faerie Mastermind, Kefnet the Mindful

Two are Defenders bought purely to block (Angelic Wall {1}{W}, Drift of Phantasms {2}{U}). Kefnet carries a live condition — he 'can't attack or block unless you have seven or more cards in hand', which Reliquary Tower, Decanter of Endless Water and The Second Doctor's no-maximum-hand-size clauses exist to keep true.
engines.evidence: cards.json oracle enumeration (6 of 18 creatures fly, 0 have reach); sim n120: of heliod's 74 eliminations, giada-angels caused 39 and 53 were eliminated_how 'damage'; heliod's combat_damage_taken mean 36.08, median 24.0. goldfish target 'A body that can block a FLIER' assembles 0.750, 0.604 by turn six

engines.piece: Lightning Greaves, Guardian of Faith, Karametra's Blessing, Teferi's Protection, Leyline of Anticipation
engines.engine: Commander insurance, and Cullen's taxonomy as quoted in strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance maps onto it cleanly: constant protection (Lightning Greaves — haste and shroud, equip {0}), single-use instants (Guardian of Faith phases out other creatures you control; Karametra's Blessing gives an ENCHANTMENT CREATURE hexproof and indestructible, which Heliod is on both faces; Teferi's Protection phases your whole board), and a route that does not need him at all (Leyline of Anticipation duplicates the flash grant).
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; sim n120 commander_access: casts mean 0.69 (max 3), games_resolved 68 of 120, resolved_rate 0.567, first resolution at global turn 34.5 on the mean. goldfish target 'Heliod protected, or a flash grant that does not need him' assembles 0.680, 0.526 by turn six

engines.piece: Counterspell, Swan Song, An Offer You Can't Refuse, Dovin's Veto, Arcane Denial, Archmage's Charm, Force of Negation, Fierce Guardianship
engines.engine: The counter wall — 8 of the 21 answer cards, two of them free. strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite's note that 'counterspells do both jobs' is why the answers-to-answers budget is not a separate eight slots here: the same cards protect the Approach turn and stop the table's win.
engines.evidence: card_roles histogram via deck-facts: counterspell 8, removal:spot 4, protection:self 5, removal:sweeper 2, removal:bounce 1, removal:damage 1 = 21; benchmark.json response: answer_cards 21, answer_share 0.25, classes_covered 6 of 15. goldfish 'Free or cheap interaction held' assembles 0.843, 0.707 by turn six, but interaction_castable is only 0.626 at turn six against 0.927 in hand

engines.piece: Day of Judgment, Supreme Verdict, Cyclonic Rift
engines.engine: The reset. Two wraths plus an overloaded Rift, which is the deck's answer to a board it cannot block. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math's Commander correction cuts the other way here — you are the player casting it, and the section's advice 'let another player's board be the reason it gets cast' is the political cover the fort buys you.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; deck-facts roles: removal:sweeper 2. Rebuild route: Heliod's front-face ETB returns 'target enchantment card that isn't a God from your graveyard to your hand' and cards.json holds 9 non-God enchantments (Dictate of Kruphix, Forced Fruition, Ghostly Prison, Leyline of Anticipation, Mystic Remora, Propaganda, Rhystic Study, Smothering Tithe, Teferi's Ageless Insight). Note: all three sweepers are `invisible` in `model-coverage heliod` — the goldfish has no opponent, so it cannot price them at all

engines.piece: Stroke of Genius, Braingeyser, Prosperity, Skyscribing, Mathemagics, Secure the Wastes, Walking Ballista, Hangarback Walker
engines.engine: The X-spell sinks the discount pays for. Heliod's back face reduces generic cost, so an {X} spell's fixed part shrinks and X grows — and Prosperity, Skyscribing and Mathemagics feed the discount for the SAME turn by drawing the whole table. Four X-cost cards turn spare mana into a body — Secure the Wastes, Mikaeus the Lunarch, Hangarback Walker and Walking Ballista (enumerated from cards.json: nine cards carry {X} in their mana cost, and those four are the ones that leave a permanent behind).

engines.piece: Mystical Tutor, Enlightened Tutor, Long-Term Plans, Drift of Phantasms (transmute)
engines.engine: Four routes back to the second Approach and to the fort. Mystical Tutor puts it on top; Long-Term Plans puts any card third from the top at instant speed; Enlightened Tutor finds an artifact or enchantment. Drift of Phantasms is the one the role taxonomy nearly misses: transmute {1}{U}{U} finds any mana-value-3 card, and cards.json holds 16 others at that cost — including Rhystic Study, Propaganda, Ghostly Prison, Teferi's Protection, Fierce Guardianship and Force of Negation.

candidate_missing_lines.title: The second Approach cast at an opponent's end step under Heliod's flash grant
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Heliod's back face reads 'You may cast spells as though they had flash', so Approach — a sorcery — can be cast in the window strategy:tempo.sequencing recommends ('committing at the end step before your own turn so the table's chances to respond are spent'). Verified stack 002 resolves the win check but its board has no flash grant and no held counter, so the sequencing question it settles is the sorcery-speed one. Whether the free-counter backup (Fierce Guardianship's alternative cost needs a commander on the battlefield) is live in that same window depends on Heliod still being there, which sim n120 says he is in only 0.567 of games.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Karametra's Blessing saving Heliod: does the enchantment-creature rider apply on both faces, and what does it fail to stop?
cards: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse

The load-bearing negative is what indestructible does not cover: exile and bounce still remove him, and 'destroy all creatures' from Day of Judgment is answered while Supreme Verdict's is too. A scenario should also settle the Lightning Greaves conflict below.

cards: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Greaves grants shroud, which stops YOUR targeting too — Karametra's Blessing targets a creature and Guardian of Faith's ETB targets 'other target creatures you control'. Equip {0} means the Greaves can move off in response, but only at sorcery speed. Two of the four protection slots may therefore be mutually exclusive with the third while equipped, which would change how the goldfish's 0.680 'Heliod protected' target should be read.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Guardian of Faith phasing the board out of a wrath, and what happens to a transformed Heliod
cards: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Guardian of Faith has Flash and an ETB that phases out 'any number of other target creatures you control', which is a one-card fog against a sweeper — the resilience strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math prefers over restraint. Two unsettled points: whether a phased-out Heliod returns on his TRANSFORMED face, and whether the Guardian itself (not 'other') survives. Nothing in stacks/ covers phasing.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Heliod's discount and an {X} spell: how much does the table's draw step actually cut?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: The discount is '{1} less for each card your opponents have drawn THIS TURN', so it is largest on your own turn only if opponents drew during it — Font of Mythos and Howling Mine fire on each player's draw step, not yours. That suggests the discount is at its maximum on an OPPONENT'S turn, which is exactly when the flash grant lets you cast. A scenario should count the reduction precisely and confirm it floors at the coloured pips. `model-coverage` shows the goldfish does not model this channel at all, so no artifact currently answers it.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Drift of Phantasms transmute as a fort tutor
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Transmute {1}{U}{U} discards Drift to search for a card with the same mana value (3). Enumerated from cards.json, 16 other nonland cards in this 99 cost 3, including Propaganda, Ghostly Prison and Rhystic Study (Archangel of Tithes is mana value 4 and out of range). That would make the lowest-assembling defensive target ('A taxer down', 0.487) materially more reliable — but transmute is sorcery-speed only and costs the blocker, and the goldfish's tutor model counts it as filling one any_of group without pricing that tradeoff.

matchup_frames.vs_the_standard_pod: MEASURED, and it is the best evidence this deck has. Sim run giada-angels-vs-baylen-tokens-vs-abaddon-n120 (Forge 2.0.14, 120 games, 4 seeded jobs, 600s clock, three bracket-3 opponents): heliod 27 wins, win_rate 0.252, CI95 [0.180, 0.342]; 12 games truncated and 1 drawn, so 108 decided. An even share of the decided games across four seats is 108/120/4 = 0.225, which sits inside that interval — the run does NOT separate this deck from an even split, and the point estimate is what ranks it. On the same pod: ur-dragon 0.305 [0.222, 0.404] (n=100), heliod 0.252 (n=120), edgar-vampires 0.144 [0.088, 0.228] (n=100), zur-enchantress best-of-four 0.118 (n=60), goblin-storm 0.031 (n=100). Second by point estimate; the marginal intervals overlap and no interval on a DIFFERENCE has been computed, so that ordering is not a separation. STALENESS: the run's heliod seat carries decklist_sha256 decc32b080fe — V6/v1.0.0, which the record's own note says held 14 Islands to 3 Plains. The current list is 214af3084f80. Every Forge figure in this frame therefore describes the deck one version ago; the goldfish, benchmark, diagnostic and mana figures all match the current sha.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: This is the matchup that kills you and it has a name: giada-angels caused 39 of heliod's 74 eliminations, and 53 of them were eliminated_how 'damage'. combat_damage_taken mean 36.08, median 24.0 against combat damage dealt of mean 4.11, median 0.5. strategy:combat-math.racing's Commander correction is the ruling: 'you cannot race three life totals' — so you do not race, you tax and you block. Two layers, and neither is reliable yet. The tax layer (Propaganda, Ghostly Prison, Archangel of Tithes) assembles in 0.487 of goldfish games and 0.355 by turn six — the lowest of the four defensive targets. The block layer is six fliers and zero reach, enumerated from cards.json, at 0.750 assembled and 0.604 by turn six — and one of the six (Kefnet) cannot block below seven cards in hand. strategy:card-advantage.virtual is why the tax layer is worth more per slot than the blockers: a taxer blanks three attack plans, a Wall blanks one attacker.
matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: You are on the right side of strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math and should behave that way: 'against a control deck, holding back often IS the loss, because buying time is exactly their plan' — but that is advice to the deck being wrathed, and here the mirror correction is that your board is not your plan. deck-facts counts 18 threat:body cards, yet sim n120 gives creatures_lost a mean of 1.33 with median 0.0 and first_attack_turn a mean of 21.12 across only 60 of 120 games: this deck barely commits and barely attacks. A rival wrath costs you the fort, not the win. Rebuild through Heliod's front-face ETB, which returns any of the 9 non-God enchantments in the list from the graveyard. The real risk against another control deck is the counter war on the Approach turn — strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window's standard applies to you: 'assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing.' Verified stack 002 makes the constraint exact: the stack is the ONLY window.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Your worst structural matchup, and strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial says why in one sentence: 'Decks built on many cheap spells per turn are hit hardest: taxes attack the velocity math directly.' This deck's curve is 12 one-drops and 21 two-drops (deck-facts) and its plan is several cheap permanents per turn plus held-up counters. It also forces the role: 'you rarely own the long game under an assembling lock, so you are the beatdown, racing the lock's completion.' That is the one board state where the inevitability read above INVERTS. Two live outs, both castable under most taxes: Disenchant, Loran of the Third Path and Cathar Commando answer artifact and enchantment lock pieces, and Cyclonic Rift overloaded resets a lock built out of permanents. Name the piece that beats YOU — the one that stops Approach or stops your draw — not the scariest one (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy).
matchup_frames.vs_combo: You are the table's answer-holder, and strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy names the countervailing risk plainly: 'held answers rot — against combo, or lethal already on board, the last profitable moment is now.' Eight counterspells is the right suite for this and the free ones (Force of Negation, Fierce Guardianship) are what let you hold up nothing and still say no — though Fierce Guardianship's alternative cost needs your commander on the battlefield, and sim n120 says he is there in 0.567 of games. The measured worry is not the count but the mana: goldfish interaction_in_hand is 0.927 at turn six while interaction_castable is 0.626 — you are HOLDING answers you cannot pay for a quarter of the time, and that figure is a floor because the model spends everything every turn. The gift engine is also a liability here: Forced Fruition hands a combo deck seven cards per spell, and Howling Mine and Font of Mythos accelerate their assembly as much as your discount.

distribution_notes: 100 copies in 85 entries: 67 nonland, 33 lands in 18 entries (deck-facts). CURVE, against strategy:deckbuilding.curve's EDHREC baseline of 15.7 two-drops and 15.4 three-drops in the average deck — 2 zero-drops, 12 ones, 21 twos, 17 threes, 9 fours, 2 fives, 2 sixes, 1 seven, 1 eight. This deck is well above the format at two and three and nearly empty above four; the nine four-drops match the section's observation that builders run more cards at their commander's mana value. The six cards above mana value four, enumerated from cards.json, are Alhammarret's Archive and Psychosis Crawler at five, Consecrated Sphinx and Forced Fruition at six, Approach at seven and Dig Through Time at eight — and Dig delves, so its printed cmc overstates what you pay. The section's discipline — 'you're probably only going to be able to cast ONE big-mana spell per game' — is why Approach at {6}{W} is the expensive card the deck is built to pay for, and why the rest of the top end is X-spells that scale. MANA. 33 lands is below strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base.color-sources' assumption (Karsten's 99-card column assumes 40), and it shows: mana_analysis gives 25 W sources and 26 U against its own source_targets of 36 each, and on-curve probability lands-only of 0.610 W / 0.639 U, 0.718 / 0.742 with rocks, 0.580 / 0.610 once Skycloud Expanse is excluded as gated. Karsten's 'consistently' means about 90%. Read against his table the shortfall is concrete: the commander is 2{W}{W} (26 sources wanted, 25 held) and Archangel of Tithes is 1{W}{W}{W} (33 wanted). 7 lands enter tapped, 2 of them always — inside his cap of about four taplands. goldfish land_drop_hit_rate falls 0.729 / 0.603 / 0.540 across turns four to six and benchmark's missed_land_drop_rate is 0.2532 with turn six the worst; diagnostic puts missed_land_drop_by_five at 0.5194 and reports the deck ABOVE the fleet median on mana. Stalling is nonetheless rare after turn one (two-turns-in-a-row 0.0091, below the fleet median), and 786 of 792 stall turns were mana_short rather than hand_empty — hand-empty accounts for 6 of the 792, so the constraint is lands and not cards. KEEPS. goldfish opening_hand: 0.734 of first sevens are kept, mean_mulligans 0.333, and 0.981 of kept hands can act by turn three. strategy:mulligans.engine-hands' Commander correction is the right reading of that 0.734 — 'the customary free first mulligan makes the first ship near-free — use it ruthlessly — and 100-card singleton means you mulligan to enabler *classes*, not named cards'. The classes here are a land pair, a cheap draw-for-the-table permanent, and one answer; the deck has 11 permanent routes to the first, so keeping for a NAMED card is never correct except for Approach itself. ROLES (deck-facts, coverage 0.8588; 12 cards have no pattern, which is absence of a pattern and not absence of the function): draw:engine 9, draw:burst 5, draw:wheel 5, threat:body 18, counterspell 8, removal:spot 4, removal:sweeper 2, removal:bounce 1, removal:damage 1, protection:self 5, ramp:rock 7, ramp:cost-reduction 3, tutor:unrestricted 2, tutor:narrow 2, wincon:alt 1, wincon:drain 2. Against strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite's counts — Walser's 8-10 removal inside a 15-20 card interactive suite, wipes 'one or two max' — the 21-card suite is at the top of the range and the 2 wraths are correct, but breadth is 6 of 15 classes (benchmark.json), and the section puts breadth before depth: 'cover the classes — creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land — before doubling any.' There is no graveyard answer in the 99. THREAT DENSITY. strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density asks for 3-5 finishers and this deck has ONE: Approach. The 18 threat:body cards are blockers and mana sinks, not finishers — sim n120's first_attack_turn mean of 21.12 over 60 of 120 games says the bodies do not convert. That is the ceiling-versus-median tradeoff the section names, taken to its limit: 'the ceiling build runs one spectacular finisher and loses when it's answered.' The 7 attrition wins in the sim run are the deck closing without it. MODEL COVERAGE. 78 seen, 0 dark, 7 invisible (Cyclonic Rift, Day of Judgment, Dig Through Time, Disenchant, Path to Exile, Supreme Verdict, Swords to Plowshares) — the goldfish has no opponent, so the entire removal suite is unpriced there, and Heliod's cost discount is unmodelled. diagnostic.json's engine section is unavailable because no goldfish target is marked `required: true`, so this deck has no measured engine lift.
overall_assessment: This deck does not build a board to win with; it builds a board to not die behind, and it wins with a card that says 'you win the game'. The world-view is strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock's — 'four-player games trend long, so inevitability compounds' — and the deck owns the long game on two of the four sources that section lists: an unanswerable finisher and more answers than the table has threats. The mechanism is a deliberate inversion. Eleven permanents hand the whole table cards, which reads as generosity and is priced as one (strategy:multiplayer.politics, and strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection's 'engines that read as defensive'). Then Heliod, the Warped Eclipse charges you {1} less per card they drew and lets you cast at instant speed; Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Smothering Tithe and Consecrated Sphinx make the symmetric gift asymmetric; Psychosis Crawler and Scrawling Crawler bill them for taking it; and Propaganda, Ghostly Prison and Archangel of Tithes make attacking you the worst-value attack at the table. The pilot's own summary is the same claim in plainer words: 'we don't win through combat; we control, we survive, we enchant and tutor. we cast second sun twice, and our board state is designed to keep us alive.' The measurement agrees with the theory more cleanly than usual. Over 120 Forge games against three bracket-3 opponents the deck won 27 (0.252, CI95 [0.180, 0.342]) with a mean finishing position of 2.319 over 94 ranked games, and 20 of those 27 wins were the Approach effect while 7 were the last seat standing — the deck is doing on the table exactly what it says on paper. It got there dealing a MEDIAN of 0.5 combat damage and reaching 21 commander damage in zero games. What the same run says about the limits is why fourteen cards changed: the deck was eliminated in 74 of 120 games, 53 of those to damage, 39 of them by one opponent 31 of whose 32 creature cards carry flying (enumerated from data/opponents/giada-angels/decklist.txt against cards.csv; the lone exception is Starnheim Aspirant) — and the current 99 answers that with five new defensive slots and a commander-protection package, because Heliod resolved in only 0.567 of games and averaged 0.69 casts. Two honest holes remain. The first is that this is a ONE-finisher deck where strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density asks for three to five, and the fallback is not a second combo — the pilot has ruled that out — but attrition, which the sim shows works about a quarter as often as Approach. The second is that the fort the whole plan rests on is the least reliable of the four defensive targets: 'A taxer down' assembles in 0.487 of goldfish games and only 0.355 by turn six, while the gift engine that helps everyone is online in 0.935 by mean turn 2.319. Until those two rates converge the deck is, for several turns each game, handing three opponents cards from behind a door that is not yet locked. And there is a posture risk the doc names directly. strategy:resource-hedging opens on it: 'playing not to lose' prioritizes delaying defeat over maximizing win probability, and it is mathematically wrong — the distinction being that playing SAFE is correct from ahead while playing SCARED pays real equity to dodge specific cards. A deck whose median combat damage is 0.5 and whose mean finishing position is 2.319 is a deck that is very good at coming second. The section's rule of thumb is the correction to hold in mind at the table: hedge from ahead, gamble from behind — and the gamble here is casting the second Approach into a table that might have the counter, rather than waiting for a turn that never gets safer.
gaps: NO SECTION ON ALTERNATE WIN CONDITIONS. A card that reads 'you win the game' is a different object from a threat: it cannot be blocked, raced or removed once resolving, and the entire skill is the one window on the stack. Querying 'you win the game alternate wincon protecting the win spell' returns strategy:resource-hedging at 0.407 and nothing on topic. This deck's whole plan has no home in the doc. Wanted: how to time a win-the-game spell across three responders, how many tutors and protection slots one is worth, and the two-cast structure (Approach, Thassa's Oracle, Coalition Victory, Test of Endurance) as a class.

NO SECTION ON PILLOW-FORT / DETERRENCE ECONOMICS. strategy:card-advantage.virtual has one clause about tax effects blanking three attack plans and that is the whole of it; the query 'pillow fort deterrence tax attackers Propaganda Ghostly Prison' tops out at 0.241. Wanted: how many taxers a fort needs before it is a deterrent rather than a speed bump, how {2}-per-attacker prices against a token deck versus a Voltron deck, and why an untaxable route (fliers, trample, direct damage) breaks the whole layer at once.

NO SECTION ON SYMMETRICAL RESOURCE GIFTS (group hug as a means, not an end). Feeding the table to power your own discount, taxes and drains is a real archetype and this deck IS one; the doc treats card advantage only as asymmetry. Wanted: when the gift is net-positive, what conversion rate makes it so, and the failure mode where the cards you handed out kill you (here: Forced Fruition against a combo seat).

NO SECTION ON EVASION AXES AND BLOCKER COVERAGE. The doc has strategy:combat-math but nothing on how to cover flying, menace, trample and unblockable in the 99 — the query returns 0.175 at best. This deck just spent five slots on the flying axis alone off a measured elimination count, and had no framework to size that decision against.

NO SECTION ON THE DRAW-GO POSTURE. strategy:tempo.sequencing covers ordering within a turn and strategy:multiplayer.pod-management notes that open mana 'forces three players, not one, to respect your possible interaction', but nothing addresses how much mana to leave up across a four-player turn cycle, or when to break the posture and develop. The goldfish measures the gap (interaction in hand 0.927 versus castable 0.626 at turn six) and the doc cannot advise on it.

bracket_report.json IS STALE and should be regenerated before any power-level claim is made from it. Enumerated against the current cards.json: of its 10 listed Game Changers, 8 remain (Consecrated Sphinx, Cyclonic Rift, Enlightened Tutor, Fierce Guardianship, Mystical Tutor, Rhystic Study, Smothering Tithe, Teferi's Protection) and 2 are gone (Ancient Tomb, Drannith Magistrate). The 120-game Forge run predates the current decklist (seat sha decc32b080fe against the current 214af3084f80, a difference the run's own note describes as 14 Islands to 3 Plains). A re-run on 214af3084f80 is what would tell us whether the five defensive additions changed the 39-of-74 elimination share, and it is the single highest-value measurement this deck is missing.

goldfish_targets.json HAS A MEMBERSHIP DEFECT that inflates two figures. The any_of group for 'Table draw engine online (opponents are drawing)' and the one for 'Engine + punisher assembled' both list Decanter of Endless Water, whose oracle text in cards.json and in the corpus is 'You have no maximum hand size. {T}: Add one mana of any color' — it makes nobody draw. It is correctly a member of the 'mana to flip him' group. Until it is removed from the two draw groups, the 0.935 / 0.854 / mean-turn-2.319 assembly figures count games where the only 'engine' drawn was a mana rock, and the same overcount flows into 'Engine + punisher' 0.334.
